utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We have some matters to deal with before we hear evidence from the witnesses. On the 4th of September, the Prosecution made use of a logbook or medical protocol book from the Visegrad health centre during its examination of Witness VG-032. On the 3rd of October, the Prosecution notified the Chamber that there was some confusion as to whether the entire logbook had been admitted into evidence as Exhibit P68 or whether only two pages of the logbook comprised Exhibit P68. The logbook in question contains some 400 pages and was admitted in the Vasiljevic case. However, in the Chamber's view, most of the information in it is irrelevant to the present case. In order to clarify the record, the Chamber rules that the pages of the logbook which contain entries made on the 7th of June, 1992, are admitted into evidence as Exhibit P68 under seal. These pages which are unredacted are those numbered as 0545-2073 and 0545-2074, and these pages in their redacted form are admitted as Exhibit P70. I take this opportunity to clarify that Exhibit 1D39 only comprises pages of the logbook which contain entries of 14th June 1992. These pages are those numbered as 0545-2111 and 0545-2112. The parties will recall that the question of in-court or doc identification has arisen in this case on some occasions. I would like written submissions from the parties by the -- I see here the 31st of October, but that can't be right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. I'd like written submissions from the parties by the 31st of October on how in-court or doc identification is to be treated. The submission should take account of the decisions of the Appeals Chamber, as well as case law from other jurisdictions. The Trial Chamber is particularly interested in the following questions: One, what constitutes in-court or doc identification? Two, does it include a situation where the witness knows the accused before the incident? Three, in considering how it is to be treated, an issue arises as to whether doc identification goes to weight or admissibility, so I'd like submissions on that. Four, in circumstances where it is determined that there is a case of doc identification, how is that evidence to be treated on a no-case submission under Rule 98 bis. In particular, should the Defence be called on to respond to that evidence. An issue here is that in the regime for no-case submissions at the Tribunal, in order to succeed one has to show that there is no evidence capable of supporting a conviction on a count as a whole and that seldom is the case. In the instant case, a point to be considered is whether there is evidence other than the doc identification supporting a count. When I mentioned earlier the date of the 31st of October for the submissions, I paused because I thought it wasn't enough time, but on reflection I think it is enough time. Mr. Alarid, I see -- I am informed that you are -- you're now fortified, much better resourced, and I see you smiling. You have a co-counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I do, Your Honour, and that was going to be the first thing -- that was going to be the first order of business is, of course, to introduce as formal co-counsel Mr. Dan Ivetic to the Court as he has been appointed as of 5.00 p.m. Thursday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: So we are fortified to a certain degree, although are still making concessions with our team due to the fact of we're level 1 at this juncture and still needing resources in the field, and so it's still a problem, Your Honour. I can't say it's been resolved, but I at least have the support in the courtroom and I think the Court wanted for purposes ever continuity but it still is a process.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, the Chamber takes the opportunity to welcome Mr. Ivetic, and we note the familiarity that he has with the case, and we are confident that he will be of tremendous help to the Defence. The third matter I wanted to raise --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I was saying that I wanted to raise another matter, and it has to do with the motion filed by Milan Lukic to suppress the testimony for failure of timely disclosure with Confidential Annexes A and B. This is in reference to the testimony of VG-114. Mr. Groome, you will notice that in the motion, in paragraph 3 there are references to six batches of disclosures that have been made within a week, and the Chamber would be assisted to be informed what these batches relate to. We would be in a better position to decide on the motion if we were informed what the batches of evidence are -- relate to and so we would want you to give us that information at the very earliest opportunity.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, when this issue first arose, I gave the Chamber some information. I can recall for the Chamber what I advised the Chamber at that stage, but I will take advantage of the first break to get more detailed information, but much of the -- much of the documents related to prior reports of the -- of the experts. If you recall, that week there were several experts that testified. And some of it was also in relation to -- there was some of these reports that we did not believe were disclosable under the rules but nevertheless may have been of interest to the Defence, and we sent them a letter stating this and saying we would make that material, although we did not see it as disclosable material, if it was information -- additional information that they wished to see, we would make that available to them, and both counsel accepted that offer and asked to see that material. And some of that material is also included in -- in that -- that large amount of disclosure that was made that week, but, Your Honour, I can give more precise information over the course of the break and report after the first break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. We'd like more precise information. Thank you very much, Mr. Groome. Those are the matters I wanted to deal with before the witness was called. Would you please call the witness now.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Sorry. Mr. Alarid.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We have additional preliminary matters and sort of in the same vein as the final question to Mr. Groome. You know, one of the problems that's been is that we've been forced into this timetable of getting ready for the defence and also keeping up with this schedule of trial which has also been mixed up quite a bit by refiling of witness lists and amending of the witness lists and subsequent disclosures. I will put the Court on notice that just on Thursday, just after 5.00 p.m., we get an e-mail saying shortly will be in your locker batch 47. Well, batch 47 constitutes 53 documents, and of those 53 documents that actually consist of over a thousand pages, and the thousand pages is -- some of them are for the newly tendered handwriting expert, but all of these -- and this not exhaustive because we've actually gone through these and put 19 of the 53 documents that were in this stack away in binders that were set for the witnesses to be called during this -- as we restart the case. Now, the thing is these are all things that could have been given to us at the beginning of the two weeks, maybe that Friday afternoon that we had that short hearing, but instead it's until after business on Thursday right before the weekend. And so what we've had to do this weekend is go through as much as we could, file as much away in the witness binders that we could, and we still have all of this to go through. Some of it's in B/C/S. Some of it's English with no B/C/S translation. Some of it's English with no B/C/S. And so it puts us at an incredible disadvantage because of these 53 documents several of them are considered to be Rule 68. Some of them are considered to be Rule 66, and we're dealing with this all at the twelfth hour. And it's tantamount to, you know, a large insurance firm back in the States papering people at the last minute and giving you that needle in the haystack to find, if -- unless there's enough time reasonably to go through the documents, and I mean this is a lot of paper work to go through and shuffle especially with our staff as limited as it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Groome, why are you drowning the Defence with paper?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, there's certainly no intentional effort to drown anyone. Our only intention is to abide by the requirements that the Rules impose on us. With respect to the handwriting expert, the Chamber hasn't even added him or granted us the right to add him yet, so we thought -- our thought we were being as cooperative as possible as soon as we identified him as a potential witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: It's the timeliness that's the issue. Why do they get it so late and so many pages?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: With respect to the handwriting expert, which I think is an awful large portion of this, we've just filed a motion last week to -- or I forget the exact date when it was filed but we filed a motion to add him. I asked my staff to go through and check -- do and computer search on him, see what other cases he's testified in and to gather that and to present that to the Defence as soon as possible. The other material that Mr. Alarid is referring to I'm not exactly sure. I know there was no effort to intentionally give it to him after the weekend. In fact, when the witnesses that are testifying today, when they made statements that we thought were discoverable after they arrived here in The Hague, that was -- every effort was made to contact me at my home to authorise the disclosure to Mr. Alarid yesterday evening. So we've made every effort to get material to Mr. Alarid as soon as possible. If we have failed somewhere, I would want to know about that and I'll do whatever I can to correct it but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: There is a distinction between 68 material and 66(A)(ii) because 66(A)(ii) ought really to have been disclosed long ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, with respect to the handwriting, let's really think about what we're speaking about. We're talking about a handwriting expert who is not on the witness list yet, so I made efforts last week to try to --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Please slow down for the interpreters. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I apologise -- to assist Mr. Alarid even before the Prosecution case to identify the Rule 66 material for the handwriting expert and to provide that as soon as possible. That is a large part of what Mr. Alarid is now referring to. The other materials that he's referring to, I'm not even precisely sure whether there's any Rule 66 material related to these two witnesses. I will say to the Chamber that as soon as we are able, and we're competing with other trial cases to have computer searches done of the 7 million-plus documents, if in those searches additional material is revealed that is considered Rule 66, we disclose that immediately, Your Honour. So again I will take a look at exactly what was disclosed on Thursday, but I can assure the Chamber there's been absolutely no intentional effort to -- to put Mr. Alarid at a disadvantage. Every effort has been made to get him this material as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I could just add to that, I could maybe clear things up with at least the handwriting expert portion of it. If we could simply know from the Prosecution if they will be doing this again Friday of this week because the time-limits for the objections under 94 bis to the expert of course flow from when the material is provided to the Defence, so we need to know that in order to plan our resources. As for the other documents, I do have the index that was in disclosure batch 47 and again --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would the counsel please slow down for interpretation. Slow down for the interpreters and, please, the interpreters could not follow at this speed. And please repeat the last three sentences. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: One of our main concerns is that the disclosure batch 47 was named just that, disclosure batch 47. The e-mail sent by the Office of the Prosecutor did not even have an index of the documents to allow us to ascertain what material was in the locker at 6.00 in the evening on the weekend. We would ask that the Prosecution at least show us the courtesy of advising us what documents are being dumped into a locker particularly where deadlines under the Rules, and again counsel cited compliance to the Rules, and we want to ensure that we comply with the Rules, and in order to comply with the Rules, we need the assistance to know when dates for responses and the like come into play. I do have the said index of disclosure batch 47 with me because it's in the binder with the expert, and I can affirm that indeed in addition to the material for the handwriting expert much of the other material, if not a majority of the other material, is listed as Rule 66(A) material. So it's not a case where it's only the expert that is Rule 66(A) material, albeit I don't know if it's pertaining to the witnesses scheduled this week or not, but I did want to bring that to the Court's attention and that could be verified just by pulling up the index which identifies the reasons for disclosure for the documents and it's chocked full with Rule 66, Rule 66 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would the counsel please slow down for interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You used a very loaded term, Mr. Ivetic, "dumped." The documents are being "dumped."

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I -- and appropriately or not, they just got dumped off the table. I apologise if there's any misunderstanding there. I just consider -- in the American vernacular when materials are put somewhere without an identification of what is in those materials, we commonly used the term "dumped" as opposed to being delivered because you don't know what's in that packet until you go there and physically go through it. I apologise if there's any confusion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Groome would have heard what you said. We are going to be considering the motion filed, and Mr. Groome is going to provide the additional information that the Chamber sought as quickly as possible. We should move to the witnesses now.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution calls VG-042. Mr. Travis Farr, he has not appeared before in this trial, he will be taking this witness. Your Honour, I'd like to raise a matter with respect to protective measures. On the 20th of June, 2008, the Chamber issued protective measures for this witness which included a pseudonym, facial distortion and voice distortion. After discussing it with the witness after her arrival here in The Hague, she believes she no longer needs voice distortion, so I would ask for an amendment to the protective measures order and I think that would facilitate the taking of her testimony if there is no voice distortion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We grant that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, while we're waiting for the witness, may I update you on VG-024, that was the witness that was the subject of a subpoena. VG-024 has considered her position and has now agreed to voluntarily come to The Hague and she'll be arriving here in The Hague on the 1st of November.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: So the softly, softly approach worked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Please read the declaration to the witness, and the witness will repeat it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Witness, please repeat after me. I solemnly declare.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That I will speak the truth.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That I will speak the truth.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The whole truth.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The whole truth.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: And nothing but truth.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And nothing but the truth alone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. You may now commence. I'm sorry I didn't get your name properly.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Travis Farr appearing for the Prosecution today, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Travis Farr.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Your Honour, can we briefly move into private session to take the personal details of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Witness 042, what is your ethnic or religious background?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: I'm a Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Can you describe for us generally where you lived in 1992? Not your specific house address but in what area.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: Dusce, Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Are you familiar with the Varda furniture factory in Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: Yes. It's right outside my door.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Before the war, did you know a couple named Dzemal Zukic and Behka Zukic and their family?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: Of course. They were my neighbours.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Did some people call Behka by another name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: They called her Behija.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Do you know which of these names was her real name and which one was her nickname?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: I think her real name was Behija, and Behka was more of a nickname.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know how this family earned a living before the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: They got married when they were young. They left for Germany. Then once there, they got their lives back up and running. They owned a shop that they ran, and I think they had a decent life.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Did this family own any vehicles before the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: Yes. Well, I don't know. I don't really know, because soon after they were married they left for Germany. When they returned from Germany, they had a TAM truck and a passenger vehicle, a Passat.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Do you know what, if anything, happened to this Passat during the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Can you please tell the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: Sure. One day I went to the MUP building in town to get a pass to leave town just to make sure we were safe. I was on my way back to Dusce. There were two roads. One was next to the Drina River; it was an asphalt road, surfaced. And then there was a macadam road parallel to the rail line, so we took that road in order not to meet any Chetniks on our way back. As soon as I reached the Varda furniture factory, there's a house there belonging to a man named Sevko Hodzic. Dzemo Zukic and his Behija passed us, and then there was a white Fico driving behind us and it pulled over right outside Sevko Hodzic's house. Milan Lukic got out of that Fico vehicle and walked up to Vico [as interpreted] Zukic and his wife Behija. He seized their car. We walked on past the Varda factory to our homes. I said, Dzemo, my dear, what was that? And Behija told me one thing, Don't ask a question. Milan Lukic just took my car away. And that was that. We talked no more. We went our separate ways. We walked on, and then I took a turn towards my house, and they just walked on towards their home.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Thank you. I believe that you just said: "Dzemo Zukic and his Behija and passed us, and then there was Fico driving ..." Just to clarify, when they passed you, did they pass on foot or in an auto or how?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: They got into the car and they got pulled right over. The Fico drew up and then they pulled over too. I happened to come by. I kept my head low. I took off my shoes because I was too scared to walk on with my shoes on. I held the shoes in my hands. I was too afraid. I didn't even dare to look there. I just kept my head down and walked straight on.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: You've just mentioned that the Zukics told you that their car was taken by Milan Lukic. Had you known Milan Lukic before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: Yes, I knew Milan Lukic when he was a small boy, when he was a schoolboy. He went to the school in Klasnik. My village was Scitarevo and his village was Rujiste. I knew him as a boy. Sometimes we would take the same bus. From the school in Klasnik, there was a co-op there and one would go to the co-op. That's what they called it. And then we would take this bus together. I -- I would get off on the next stop, and then the children would get off, and I did this countless times. I've lost track, so I did see a great deal of him back then.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Thank you. As you were growing up, did your family have any pasture land?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: Yes. We had meadows that we shared. That's where Milan lived, the village of Rujiste. These are the names our meadows Cetulje, Milan knows that full well. And then Osojnica as well. Children used to play there. They played football and they were all together. That's how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Did other families have pasture land near the pasture land of your family?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: Yes. All of our people there, back where I come from, we had pastures. Other people did too. Those were our meadows. That's how we referred to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Can you tell me some of the families that had pasture land near your family's pasture land?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: Well, I can. My own family did. A number of them Hasim Todovic, but they're all dead. Ramo Cocalic, Ismet Cocalic, Aco Cocalic, they are all neighbours of my dad. Ismet Cocalic. They all know this. Mujo Ramic, there was another man called that. It was a whole neighbourhood, really. People were meeting, and they all knew each other because they grew up together, didn't they? Our children, too, they all went to the same school.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Were there any Serb families that had pasture land near your family's pasture land?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: This question sounds me as --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just a minute, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, with your leave this question sounds me as a leading question. I think that we already received the answer from this witness about that issue. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Farr, you have to be careful about leading.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: You've mentioned that you would occasionally see Milan Lukic on the bus when he was a boy. Did you see him in any other locations when he was a boy?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: No. At school, but I maybe wouldn't have seen him that often, but I just had to go myself because I had to take care of the business. I was the eldest child and then I had to go to the co-op, which wasn't too close either, and then I had to go get some stuff and then I would meet these children on the way, you know, leaving school. And then we'd get on the bus together and drive straight on to Rujiste.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: I believe you said that Milan Lukic was from the village of Rujiste. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, that's right. That's where he was born.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Did you know any other members of his family?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: Well, I knew his mom, Kata. I knew his dad, Mile. They were on good terms with my own father. His grandfather. He was on very good terms with my father. They were close friends.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Did you --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: His name was Nedjo, Nedjo Ivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Did your father ever socialise or greet Milan Lukic's mother and father?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: Of course. What else? My father was with the -- the forestry company and then they would meet there. They'd sit down for a coffee, a brandy, that sort of thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: You've said that you know the names of Milan Lukic's parents. Did you personally greet them or socialise with them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: When I was young, a girl, a young woman, if you like, yes, we'd exchange greetings. I never stayed at their home. I can't say that I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: I believe you've mentioned Milan Lukic's primary school. Do you know where he completed the rest of his education?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: In Prlog. I think it was in Prlog, his secondary education.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: After secondary school, do you know what he did?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: I can't really say. I know he left for Serbia later on, after he'd left school. He was no longer in Visegrad. I didn't see him any more after that. I know that he was in Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Do you know whether he returns to Visegrad at some point?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: Yeah, probably he would go see his parents every now and then, but I simply didn't see him at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Returning to the day when the Zukics' car was taken from them, what happened after you parted company with them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: They drove on back to their house, further down the road from mine, and then I took a turn up the road and my home was right there. About 5.00 that afternoon the phone rings. Where are the men? Make them leave. Make them go away. They're picking up the men at Dzemo Zukic's place. (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Witness, how did you react to these phone calls that you received?

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe the witness mentioned her name again on page 18 at line 9. If that could be redacted.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: And, Witness, if I could just ask you to try to remember not to mention your name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Please make an effort. Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, with your leave, I think we missed the part which witness mentioned that the body was buried. If I say in B/C/S [B/C/S spoken]. I heard that so my learned friend can check that with additional questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: What line would that be missing from?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: 19 and 20. 19 would be. Page 18, line 19.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: I can probably clarify that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Ask that question again.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Witness, as far as you know, what happened to the body of Behka Zukic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: Well, they told me that Milan Lukic had killed her. Behija Jamak, Sabit Jamak's wife told me that.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Sorry to interrupt you, Witness. This is a slightly different question. When you arrived that morning and saw her dead body, what then happened to her body as far as you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: I know that while I was still in that house we got her body. A car drove up. I don't know what car it was. Was it an ambulance, was it not an ambulance, I don't know. I didn't look. I was too scared to look. The car took Behija Zukic's body away. And then we have a graveyard, Straziste I think is the name, and I think that's where they buried her body.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Just to clarify, though, you did not go along with the body; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: No, no, no, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: So it's just a supposition that she was taken to Straziste to be buried?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: Well, yes. Yes, that's what I believe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I think that we have some leading questions and calling for speculation in last questions. It's not a proper question for direct examination. That is my humble opinion. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I agree. Counsel, desist from leading questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Witness, a moment ago you said in reference to that morning, "Well, they told me that Milan Lukic had killed her. Behija Jamak, Sabit Jamak's wife told me that." Can you please tell the Chamber exactly what Behija Jamak told you about the death of Behija Zukic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: Sure. I can tell you everything. I know everything she told me. She told me this -- it's not just me who was there. There were other people there. She said Milan Lukic had arrived. Having taken away Faruk -- Faruk's son and Dzemo and all these other people, he drove back and he told her to give him her money and her jewellery. And she said, I have nothing left. Whatever I had I've given away. And Milan Lukic then said, Come with me to -- up to the first floor. And he said, Just sit down here. When I'm back I'll just kill you, won't I. And then she jumped out the window. There was some sort of a low-lying terrace outside the house and some meadow. And she said she was there, so they got out of the house and they left.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, is your husband alive today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Do you remember and can you describe the last day you saw him alive?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: I do remember but I don't remember the date. I know it was the Bajram when the animals were slaughtered, and he was alive until that date, and on that date he was taken away by Milan Lukic and killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Can you please describe how that happened.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: Yes, I can, and I'll do that very easily. I'll describe it easily because it's as if it was happening now before my very eyes. It was half past 10.00, and there was breakfast in the factory. People were going out for breakfast in the factory, and Milan Lukic came by with his Passat. From the car -- he parked the car at the gate, the gate where you go into the timber yard, and he stood in front of the administration building and Ramiz Karaman, a neighbour, was there and my husband was standing nearby. It was in the sawmill, actually. And he made them go towards the gate, and I was standing out on the terrace and he said to my husband -- he told him to take off his coat. I didn't hear that, but he threw his coat down on some logs and then he made them go towards the gate. And when they arrived at the gate, they stood by the car, and there was a Volvo who -- whose motor was switched on, and in the Volvo was a man called Ahmed Kasapovic. He went up to him and he knocked on the glass, made him get out of the Volvo and took him to the gate too. And when he brought them to the gate, he opened the back door and they got into the Passat, into the car and he drove them off towards town.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Thank you --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: However --

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Sorry. Just to interrupt for a moment. Just to clarify, when you say he brought them to the gate, he brought them to the back door and they got into the Passat, who are you referring to as "he"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: I'm referring to Milan Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: And after he put the three men in the back of the car, what happened next?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: He drove them off towards town, right by my house. And perhaps half an hour went by, maybe it was longer. I didn't look at my watch because I was out on the terrace all the time and felt sad, and I was screaming and crying to see what was happening, and the car came back to the same spot, the gate, and parked where it parked previously. And once again Milan Lukic got out of the car, and he walked towards the same administration building and the people were having breakfast. He rounded up the -- some people and marched them towards the gate. These were all my neighbours all these people. One was called Nusret Aljusevic, and then there was Ibrisim Memisevic. Nedzad Bektas was another. Lutvo Tvrtkovic, he was a little simple, that man. Then there was Cancar Musan.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just a minute, Witness. Now you have described two incidents in which you say Milan Lukic came and made people walk towards the car, go towards the car. How did he do this? How was he able to achieve this, to make them go to the car?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They were in front -- walking in front of him like sheep and he was walking behind them with a rifle. And then when he brought them to the gate, he took Memisevic's overalls off and they took out their cigarettes and keys and threw them down onto the overalls.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: So he had a rifle.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And was that on both occasions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. He took the three men off before, and then he came back to fetch the others.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Did -- on the first occasion, did you hear him say anything to the men? On the first occasion, did you hear Milan Lukic speak to the men and, if so, what did he say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] How do you mean did I hear him speak to him? How do you mean? I'm not quite sure what you mean.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Your Honour, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Were you in a position to -- to hear any conversation between Milan Lukic and the men?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I wasn't, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Farr.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Witness, you have just told us that Milan Lukic had gathered these six men who you named and taken them to the gate, and you also mentioned that they had -- that Ibrisim Memisevic took off his shirt and the others took out their personal items. Can you tell us what happened after that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: Yes, I can. He made them walk towards the Drina River, in front of him again, just like sheep. He herded them towards the river and he walked behind them and he brought them to the bank of the river, and I could see all this. And then he made them line up one next to the other but not too close, and then he killed them one by one. Then there was a burst of gun-fire and he killed them all. And when he came back, then he shot at us, because Ibrisim Memisevic's wife and daughter turned up and they were standing there and his daughter was shouting out, "Father, father," and he turned round when he heard this child crying. When he'd killed them down by the river, then he started shooting at us. We laid down on the ground and there were bullets whizzing by --

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: Do you want me to continue?

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Could I just ask you where you were as you were observing all of this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: I was out my terrace. Where my house is, out on the terrace.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Can you estimate the distance between your terrace and the gate that you mentioned where the workers were initially gathered?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: Yes, I can. It might be 50 as the crow flies, 50 metres, perhaps less. I can't be quite sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Did you have a clear view at the time that Milan Lukic was gathering these workers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: No, nothing occupied me. I was just -- I was just wondering how all this could happen in the middle of the day. I was astounded, and I just screamed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You'll have to ask the question again. I don't believe she understood it. What the counsel was asking you, Witness, was whether you were able to see from where you were Milan Lukic as he was gathering the workers.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I saw Milan Lukic. He was wearing a camouflage uniform. I saw him gather up the people, and I know all these people, each and every one of them. It was all happening right in front of the door from this company, and I know them all.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: And from the distance that you were watching from your terrace, could you easily recognise the victims that you've named?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: Yes. I could recognise them any time and every time. They used to come by to my house. They were all my neighbours except Cancar. He was not a neighbour, but I knew him too. He would always come by.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Can you estimate the distance between where you stood on your terrace and the point beside the river where the men were killed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: Of course I can tell you. I didn't move from my terrace. I was watching it all happen. I saw it personally from my terrace. I saw what was going on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And what was the distance between your terrace and the river? How far was your terrace from the river?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps -- well, I can't tell you exactly. I don't want to make a mistake. It might have been a hundred metres, maybe a little more, but 50 to the gate as the crow flies. Where the gate is, that's 50.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: I believe that you had also told us, Witness, that there were some other people watching these events with you on the terrace. Without using their names, can you please tell us how they reacted to these events?

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: I don't think I did, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Witness, could you estimate approximately what time of day this second event occurred, that is the taking away of the six men to the Drina.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: About 12.00. Whether it was 12.00 exactly, I can't really say. I didn't look at my watch. But it was roughly at around 12.00. It was the Bajram holiday, Kurban Bajram, the highest religious holiday. That's when that happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Could the court officer please place Prosecution Exhibit P153 on the screen, but could the director please not broadcast the image of the photo as the witness will be identifying her house. And could the usher zoom in on the centre of the photo and be available to assist the witness in marking the photo.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Witness, could you please take a look at the photograph on the screen in front of you. Do you recognise what you see in this photo? But please don't begin marking yet. Can you just describe what you see in the photo.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: Yes, I can describe it. You mean from where I was watching, from where I was standing?

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Could you just -- could you just generally tell us first what you see in the photo. Do you recognise this area? Do you recognise these buildings?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: All of this. I recognise it all. I lived there. I know it all. It's my neighbourhood. All the buildings, the houses, the sawmill, everything. I also recognise the people standing there, down there. There's a car there. Milan chased the people out in that direction, where there’s a car standing.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Do you see your house in this photo, that is the house where you were on the day that these events occurred?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Could you please circle -- do you see the veranda that you were standing on at the time these events occurred?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I see it all. I'll tell you any time you like.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Could you please circle the veranda or terrace that you were standing on at the time these events occurred?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: I'll draw circles around both terraces. The first terrace I was standing on when he took the three men away, and I'll draw a circle around the terrace that I was on when he took the other lot of people; right?

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Let me interrupt you. Could you please just circle the terrace that you were on when you saw him take the second group of people.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Thank you. And could you now mark with a cross or X the place are you saw Milan Lukic park the Passat.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Witness, are you able to make a cross or an X in that spot?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Could you now draw a line from the place where the men were gathered at the gate to the place at the river where they were killed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Can you tell us what those three lines that you've just drawn beside the river represent?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: The lines represent where he -- the point where he brought those people and where he killed them. It didn't look like this before. This is some new work that was done.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Witness, do you see the wall in the photo near the river?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: Well, yes, I can see the wall by the river, but as I say, the wall was recently built. It didn't exist before.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Your Honour, I tender Exhibit P153 as marked by this witness as a separate Prosecution exhibit under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit number P157, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Witness, did you ever try to find out what happened with your husband immediately after he was taken away?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: Of course I did. I always tried to find out what had happened, and I wasn't able to learn what had happened. It was only after a month or two. I can't say exactly how much time went by, but later people told me that they -- his body was found in the river, that the river had taken his body downstream.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: And did you ever have a chance to identify his body?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: Yes, in Visoko. That's where the identification took place. The body was in Slap, and then I transported it to Vlahovo where his body was buried.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: And how specifically was he identified?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: He was killed in the head, and I recognised him. He had some false teeth, and I made a statement and said I could recognise this. And I recognised the clothes he was wearing that day. We recognised his shirt and all the other clothing that he had on that day. We recognised all that.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: You've told us that people told you about finding his body, and you've told us about identifying his body. Did anyone ever tell you anything about how he actually died?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: Before that, I learnt about things. It was war. I went to Visoko. I was there for a year. As people came by they would say things. And then on one occasion Ramo Kurspahic was the man's name told me that he was watching across the Drina River using binoculars and that he saw my husband killed at a place called Potavnica, that they took him to that place and that that's where he was killed. So that's what I learnt from him. I learnt about it later on.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Did Ramo Kurspahic tell you who killed your husband?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: No, no, he didn't. What did I need Ramo Kurspahic to tell me when I saw that Milan Lukic took my husband away? You don't suppose he gave him to someone else to kill. He killed him.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Farr. Mr. Alarid.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Thank you Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Ms. VG-042. My name is Jason Alarid, and I represent Milan Lukic in this courtroom. Can I ask you a few questions today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, ma'am, first things first. I'd like to talk about your contact with the ICTY and giving statements regarding war crimes to either the Tribunal or to Bosnian authorities. Do you recall giving several statements to authorities in this case?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: How do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, for instance, I've received several proofing statements where you have apparently met with prosecutors and reviewed statements and given clarifications. The most recent proofing note comes from October 26th, 2008, so just a couple days ago. Do you remember giving that proofing session?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: I only say what I saw and what I know about. Nobody can influence me in any way. I tell the truth. I have children and that's why I always tell the truth and everybody should do the same. They should always tell the truth so that the truth might be known.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Ma'am, what I asked you is do you remember speaking with prosecutors, including Mr. Farr, on October 26th, 2008?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't remember everything, but I do remember -- well, I'm not literate, but I do have a clear mind, thank heaven, and I remember everything. Otherwise, I can't remember anything else. I don't remember dates. I don't know what I said today or yesterday, but I remember very well all the atrocities that took place, yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, ma'am, the 26th of October was yesterday. Do you remember speaking with Mr. Farr yesterday?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: Well, I talked to the man. I'm not sure I remember his name. I'm sure I talked to him. Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And were any -- because you're not literate, every time you have a question or want to add something to your statement were your previous statements read to you so you could clarify yourself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: I forget. Well, even if they were read out, yes, I do remember certain things, but others I forget. And whatever I do remember I recount.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, apparently yesterday, on the 26th, and I'd ask you to say if this is true or false, that in your proofing session of the 26th of October, 2008, you indicated that you now believe that Sredoje Lukic was present during the abductions at the Varda factory on 10 June 1992. Is that -- was that your statement that came to you yesterday?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And what prompted you to remember this after all this time, this belief in your -- what was told to you by -- during that proofing session if you were not able to read yourself previous statements?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: You know what led me to say that? Because Sredoje Lukic, Milan Lukic, that is to say the two children of one man, when they took the Passat from Dzemo Zukic, nobody else drew that -- drove that car, just him, and that's why I said it. Nobody ever drove that car except for the two of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But it's my understanding that this person who's in that car never got out of the vehicle so you could assess what he was wearing, how he looked. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: Well, they always wore a uniform. Perhaps I didn't express myself properly. They all wore uniforms. And he was sitting in the car, and Milan did what I've just told you about.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But, ma'am, you gave no description of Mr. Sredoje Lukic as to his age. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: I don't know what age Sredoje Lukic was exactly, but I know him well. He was a working colleague of my son, and he would come to my house often, and I knew Sredoje Lukic very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But, ma'am, you're over -- you're over 50 metres away on your veranda, and this person did not get out of a vehicle, and you gave no descriptive means for that person. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: I assume, and I always assume that Sredoje and Milan Lukic were in the car -- the Passat car together.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: So you assumed, but you do not know. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: I think that that's correct, because I would come across them before in the car. They would be there in the car together on previous occasions.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Okay. But isn't it true that the first time that you mentioned that this passenger, this passenger driver of this Passat got out of the vehicle was in the 26th of October, 2008?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: Yes, I did say that, yes. Correct. Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, you've just testified, ma'am, that you'd seen these two gentleman always in this car, always in the Passat, only them; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: Always. Nobody ever drove that car except for Milan and Sredoje. They thought it was an aeroplane, not a car. That's how they behaved.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Ma'am, do you recall going to a proofing session, your third proofing session in this matter on the 22nd of October, 2008?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And present at this proofing session was Petar Finci, Travis Farr, and Nada Kiswanson; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: Yes. It's just I didn't really memorise their names, did I.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Your Honour, just to clarify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: There is a proofing notes dated the 22nd of October, but it actually pertains to a proofing that took place on the 21st and 22nd of September. I apologise for the confusion that that might have caused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Alarid.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And, ma'am, according to this proofing note that was a clarification of a September 21st and 22nd proofing note, this indicates that you believe that the killing of Behka Zukic and the taking of her car by Milan Lukic occurred the day before the killings at the Varda factory charged in this indictment. Isn't that true, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: Maybe I got the date wrong. It was earlier on that they seized the car. It was right in front of my very own eyes. They weren't standing five metres away from me. I was right there when they did. I saw this myself. It's just that I don't really have a good head for dates at all. It's simply awful. It's very difficult. I keep having nightmares about this. You can't begin to imagine what I've seen.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, ma'am, for purposes of my questioning, you don't have to remember dates. You just have to remember sequence of events. And I think it's very specific that you would say Ms. Zukic's car was taken the day before these gentlemen were taken to the river and killed.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: I may have said that, but later on when I managed to focus, when I gave my statement and managed to focus. Was it ten days? Was it before? I really can't remember the date. I can't for the life of me. Behka was killed first and then those people were taken away, and then this incident took place.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, ma'am, those people being taken away was your husband. I would assume that you'd remember very clearly the morning your husband was taken away. Wouldn't that be true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: That's true. I remember that morning, don't I. It was just on the eve of Bajram when animals are slaughtered. I waited for my husband. He was supposed to get home for breakfast. I prepared breakfast. I was leaning over the bannister on our terrace to see when he would arrive, but what actually happened is Milan got there first, before my husband was back for breakfast. He took my husband away and Karaman Ramiz and Ahmed, Kasapovic Ahmed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But, ma'am, you should also know very well when the death of Behija Zukic occurred because you in fact saw her body and saw it taken away in a car; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. Of course I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, ma'am, if the car was taken away the day before the incident at Varda that means that you were, in fact, at Ms. Zukic's house the day your husband was taken away. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: I was there that morning. It was that morning that I was at Zukic's place to make sure we got the body into that car, and then I went back home, and I tried to whip up some breakfast. And it was at 10.30 that the incident took place involving my husband and the two men. A minute or two may have gone by, half past 10.00, breakfast-time. I was expecting my husband to show up for breakfast. I was leaning over the bannister of our terrace, waiting to sight him.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But, ma'am, according to your earlier testimony in the courtroom today, you indicated that after Ms. Zukic's vehicle was taken away that you received a call warning you that they in fact were taking away the men, being Ms. Zukic's son and husband. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: That evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And so, ma'am, if you received a call that evening --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Ma'am, if you received a call that evening, the evening of Ms. Zukic's death, before the morning that you saw her, before the morning that your husband disappeared and these other seven men were taken out, tell me, ma'am, if you received such a warning call, why would you let your husband go to work?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: Because they provided every guarantee that our men would be safe going to work. Stanko Pecikoza, for example, just seven days before this he came to my house. He had coffee with my husband. He said, "We have to work on. No work, no salary. We have to get some food. You have to go to work. You'll be safe." And that's why my husband went there, because he had received every guarantee that he'd be safe going to work.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But, ma'am, wouldn't it be fair to say that after you witnessed, supposedly the day before your husband was taken away, the seizure of Ms. Zukic's car and in fact knew about her death late that evening, don't you think things had changed enough that you wouldn't let your husband go to work?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: It's not like my husband asked me. He was the boss. It was his call, not mine. Every guarantee was provided. Not just to my husband, to all the men. They said it would be safe going to work, working on. There was every guarantee.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: What time did your husband go to work that day, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: This was June, ma'am. What time was daybreak?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: I suppose early morning, 7.00, half past 10.00 was breakfast. They worked on until 3.00 in the afternoon. That's how the company operated.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: What time did the sun come up?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: I didn't check. I didn't check for the sun coming up. I couldn't; I was asleep. It was raining that morning. When I returned from the woods, it was 7.00. When we got back my husband left for work, and I walked on to Bekija's, as I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, ma'am, according to your statement, though, it was dawn when you discovered the body of Behija Zukic. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: That morning, yes. It was after daybreak. We spent the night there. We came the next morning. We returned from the woods. This lady called me to come with her to Behka Zukic's house. It was Hajira Memisevic, so that's what I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And, ma'am, isn't it true, then, that your husband stayed with you in woods that night?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: We had spent the night in the woods, but then the next day one had to go to work, didn't one?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But, ma'am, why would he go to work after you'd actually witnessed the death of Behija Zukic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: They had told him it would be safe. We had fled Visegrad. We went to Rogatica when the -- when Sabanovic Murat said he would open the dam. And then my husband, my two daughters-in-law, and my four grandchildren left for Rogatica. I stayed behind. My mother was old and sick. So I got onto a tractor and drove as far as Medjedja, and that's how we ended up in Rogatica. Then we went back to Visegrad. A call had been published over the radio. The Serbian radio said we would be free to go back to our homes, that people should go to work, that it was safe. So that's what we did. We went back to our homes. The Uzice Corps then entered Visegrad. Some houses burned down. Thank God mine was not among them, but there were various forms of mistreatment that we suffered.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Ma'am, ma'am. That's not the question I asked you. Please try and answer the questions that I ask you, okay?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: If -- if I can get my bearings, okay, yes, that's what I'm trying to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Ma'am, I'm asking you to assume that you were, in fact, witnessing Ms. Zukic's body being taken away, and you stated on direct that you spent the night in the woods that night; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: We spent that night in the woods, yes. The next morning we went back home. My husband went to work. 7.00, that's when they started work in the factory. That was normal. Meanwhile, I went to Zukic's place to see the body and to make sure the body was driven away. And right after he'd returned from the woods my husband just went to work. That's how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And so, ma'am, are you telling me that you did not go over to Ms. Zukic's home at dawn, that you waited until your husband left to work to go?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: Yes. He went to work, and then later on I went where I went.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And what time did you -- how long did you stay at Ms. Zukic's?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: I don't know that either. I didn't check my watch. Time was not really a consideration.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: How long did you stay over there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: As I said, I wasn't checking my watch. I don't know how long. We got the body. We wrapped the body in a blanket. The body was put into a car. It was taken away, and I went back home.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: How did you get there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: Back home you mean. Just like that. It's not that it was difficult or far away.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: How far away is Ms. Zukic's home?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: Two minutes, perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Can we please call up the Prosecution Exhibit 157, please, on the e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Farr?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And actually can we have an unmarked photo which was P153 originally. And the reason I'm pausing is there -- okay. Could the court assistant assist the witness in marking this photo, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And, ma'am, the first thing I'd like you to do, again for a point of reference, is note the veranda which you were sitting on at the time you witnessed all these incidents at the Varda factory.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just a minute. Mr. Farr.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: I just ask that the photo not be broadcast since the witness will be indicating her house.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And, ma'am, who lives in that white house right next to you?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And we could go into private session if this is going to indicate location.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, ma'am, can you show me where Behija Zukic's home is on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: I can't show you that. I can't see it. It's -- you go this way to reach Behija Zukic's house. I can draw an arrow there to mark the direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Can you put the little arrow mark, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And how much further --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Alarid, we have passed the time for the break, so we're going to break now.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Alarid. Mr. Groome first.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm not sure if the Chamber wanted to note the absence of Judge Van Den Wyngaert. I look to the Chamber to ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I should have stated at the outset that at the in the absence of Judge Van Den Wyngaert, Judge David and I sit pursuant to the provisions of Rule 15 bis. Thank you, Mr. Groome. Mr. Alarid.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: As we left, I believe we had a photograph on the screen. Now, Witness 042, in referencing -- can you see the picture in front of you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: I'll just put my glasses on.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, if I understand your markings correctly, on the far right of the photograph you marked an arrow pointing off the picture to the right, our right, is in the direction of Ms. Behija Zukic; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: If you could just describe it to me. And I'd prefer how you got there personally the morning you saw the body of Behija Zukic. Describe to me how you went to Behija Zukic's home.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: I don't think I can describe that, because I took a different road from my home, because there's another path over there. So that's the one that I took.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And can you tell me how many metres past the photograph is it to Ms. Behija Zukic's home?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: It's further down. I can't show you that because it's not in the photograph. If it were in the photograph, I could point the house out for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And what I may be more curious about, could you just describe it ma'am? How many metres? How would you walk there, if you went right or left, straight ahead, that kind of thing, as if you were giving me directions to go to Ms. Zukic's home.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: I'd tell them to go in this direction, because that is the fastest way to get to Behija's house. And the other thing that I showed, it's a path that goes between the houses, and it's a shortcut of sorts.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: How long did you know Behija Zukic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: I've known Behija Zukic since we were children, since when I first moved to that village, when we were school-age children.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And so, ma'am, that's why I'm asking you. Can't you give me just simple directions on how to walk there as if I'd never been there before and you were telling me how to get there? And I'd like you to describe it. You don't need to use the photograph for this question.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: No, no need for the photograph. This is the town. You walk by the Drina River, and you arrive here. You eventually merge here, and then you take this path straight, the one that I showed you, and in no time at all you're outside her house.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now I'd like to refer you to a proofing note that we received related to September 22, 2008. Do you recall meeting with the Office of the Prosecutor back September 21st and 22nd of 2008?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: Well, whatever you ask me about that I can recall, I'll be happy to share with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, do you remember coming and meeting with the Prosecution in anticipation of testifying back in September of 2008? A little over a month ago, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: There is something I don't think I understand about this. Can you try to rephrase that maybe?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, ma'am, a little over a month ago did you have a meeting over the course of a couple of days with members of the Prosecution, proofing and where they read to you your original statements in 1993, 1994, 1998, and 2008?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: And month ago. That's what you're asking me about; right? Yes. The answer is yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And isn't it true that during those proofing sessions you were read all of your statements, all four statements? Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: Sure thing. Just ask away. I'll tell you everything I know, but I can't read and I can't write. Just ask me questions. If I know, I'll be happy to tell you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, according to the proofing statement of September 21st, 2008, you had several clarifications, namely regarding your 1993 statement and your 1994 statement. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: I don't know which statement you mean. Maybe you should clarify that so that I understand which one you mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, do you remember giving a statement to the MUP in 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: I gave several statements. I don't know who to, but that was after we had fled Visoko and then Visegrad. And it wasn't just me. Several people were giving these statements all together.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Alarid, you have used 37 minutes. The Prosecution used 40 minutes. I'll give you another ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Your Honour, that would be wholly insufficient to do a cross-examination on this witness. This witness has four prior statements. They've all been read to the statement -- excuse me, to this witness. This witness is not literate. There were several changes and clarifications to the 1993 statement of which this witness has just touched on, i.e., that she was interviewed in a group. However, the -- other than the omission or adding of names, this witness obviously describes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You tell me how much time would you need.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Those are the toughest questions you ever ask me, Your Honour, because as far as I'm concerned, it always depends on the responsive witness, the clarity of witness's recollection, as well as the willingness to just introduce these statements possibly into evidence. I would like -- although my assistant just reminded me that I need to tender the marked photo before it erases, and so I would do that. We would tender the marked photo into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We will admit it, but tell me how much time you need so I can determine how much time to --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: At least 45 minutes, Your Honour, if not an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Another 45 minutes?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: No, I am not giving that. You'll get 40 minutes, another 40 minutes. We have to be disciplined and focused.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, marked photo will become Exhibit number 1D65, under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, ma'am, you do remember giving a statement, though, in December 1993, and as you indicated some other people were present; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: How long ago was that? Sixteen years ago. Do you understand? When was that, 16 years ago? When was it that I gave that statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, ma'am, apparently in September 22nd or 21st of 2008, you remembered that Esad Gadzo and Rahima Zulic are two of the people that were with you when you gave the interview; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: So you --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: Yes, yes. That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: So you remember being there for that statement; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. That's true. I was there, and we were together.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And you made some clarifications, but other than the clarifications was everything in that 1993 statement true to the best of your ability?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: Everything I said. If that's what's written, and I wasn't there alone, it's certainly all true. You see me sitting here today, don't you? That's what it's like. I have children. I'm not say anything that's not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, in the clarification or the proofing note it indicates that the list of our neighbours who crossed over to the aggressive -- the aggressor ranks as noted on page 1 of the B/C/S version and page 2 of the English was not provided by you, and you think that it was provided by Esad Gadzo; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: No, no. That's not correct. That's not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: So you knew the names of the Chetnik neighbours that had gone over to the aggressor ranks is what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And on page 2 of the B/C/S version and page 5 of the English version, you state that you were not the one that gave the names of Brano Savovic, Risto Perisic or Drago Gavrilovic; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: Yes, correct. That was Esad Gadzo. When we gave that statement I remember that he mentioned those names. I know those people because those people are from Visegrad, but I couldn't remember the names at the time. That's right. That's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Tell us who those people were from Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Farr.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: I was just going to suggest that it might be helpful to read the applicable paragraphs of the statement to the witness in full and then put to her the question. Given that she can't read, it may be difficult for her to remember the exact context in which these lists of names were mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: We can do that, Your Honour. I would ask that we put 1D10-2087, and it's B/C/S component is 1D10-2099.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, ma'am, while we're waiting for that to come up, though, can you tell me who Brano Savovic was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: The man from Visegrad. I know him because I lived in Visegrad too. I met all those people, but I didn't spend any time with them. It's not that I was in touch with those people. Those were people who were Chetniks who were off to beat other people.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And isn't it true that Savovic was a leader in the SDS party; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: I didn't know about parties. I'm not a politician. I'm not literate. I know people when I meet them. I meet them once, I meet them twice, I know them forever.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And how did you know who Risto Perisic was, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: When Esad Gadzo and I gave a statement, I remember that clearly. He made a statement about those people, those people there, because he worked with them. He worked in the Partizan Company, and he knew more people than I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Did you know him to be the commander of the police?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: Who?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Perisic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Ma'am, when was the last time before -- you stated that you knew Milan Lukic went to Serbia, correct, after secondary school?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
