utterances.text: Yes. I didn't see him around, and I heard that he'd gone to Serbia somewhere. I don't know where, and I wasn't interested where he went, but all I know is that he wasn't in Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Before 1992, when was the last time you personally saw Milan Lukic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: I saw him when the war began in Visegrad. That's when I saw Milan Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Before the war began, ma'am. Think back before the war began. When was the last time you believe you saw Milan Lukic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: I didn't see him for some time. I told you when I saw him. I met him when he was a boy. That's when I used to see him. Then when I married I didn't see him at that time. I saw Sredoje but not Milan. I know that he went to school in Prelovo. (redacted)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: About how old was Milan when you last saw him prior to the -- to the incidents in 1992? You have told us that he was a boy. About how old was he?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He was a skinny boy, Milan Lukic, when I met him in 1992. He was very thin. I'd see him like that, thin. I'd meet him in uniform. He wore different uniforms, wasn't always in the same one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: No. We are talking now about the last time that you saw him before 1992. Before the war. And you told us that you saw him when he was a boy, so I'm asking you about how old was he at the time? About how old was he when you last saw him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, how old would a child be in fourth form? How old would a child be? Eight, ten? I don't know. He was a skinny little boy. That's how I knew him. I would be on the bus with him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, we have -- we have a little marker there, about eight or ten, and he was skinny. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And so your -- Ms. 042, are you saying that the last time when you saw him, eight or ten, you were on the bus? This was before you were married?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: Yes, yes, before I was a young girl living with my father. I hadn't married yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: All right, ma'am. I'd like to go back to the 1993 statement and take you through a few things before we get through this. According to the proofing note that the Prosecution gave me, it indicates that on page 2 of the B/C/S, page 5 of the English -- and if we could go there on the screen, please, for the Court's reference and the record. There is a list of the following citizens, the names of people, and you indicated -- or at least in the proofing notes that the witness, you, did not mention the preparation of lists of Muslims for detention and execution, but you believe that those lists existed. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: Yes, that is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And so between -- other than what we've mentioned as earlier corrections, everything else in that 1993 statement was true; correct? Up to at least page 2 of the B/C/S where we're referring to.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: Can I say something? Could you explain what you just asked me and what I said?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Okay. Ma'am, according to the statement in 1993, there is a reference that lists of Muslims -- there was a preparation of lists of Muslims for detention and execution, and according to the proofing note, you didn't say this directly, maybe one of the other two people present did, but you believe that those lists did exist. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: I'm not clear what you're asking me again. The execution of the Muslims, to have them destroyed, is that what you mean? Is that what you're telling me? That that exists? I can't really understand what you're saying. What have you just been explaining to me? I can't read. I would like it if I could read what you just said and then I could explain to you, but I'm not quite clear what you mean. Do you mean that they wanted to execute the Muslims? Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, yes, ma'am. Do you believe that to be true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: Of course. Of course they did that. That's been proved that so many Muslims were executed, killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well -- and, ma'am, according to the proofing note, page 2 of B/C/S, page 5 of the English, as -- according to the proofing note, you did not mention Savovic, Perisic, or Gavrilovic, but I would assume that you did mention Boban Tomic and Dragan Tomic; is that true?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Farr.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Could the whole sentence --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, and Sredoje Lukic and all the others.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: I think it might be easier for the witness to answer the question if the entire sentence beginning with "at the same time" --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: -- and ending with "to be executed and detained," were read to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, please do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Sure. In the English version, ma'am, and I'm reading it in English and of course it's translated to you, according to page 5 of the English translation it states: "At the same time Visegrad SDS, Serbian Democratic Party, top officials led by Brano Savovic, aged around 40, worked at the municipality in Visegrad, and his associates. "One, Risto Perisic, aged around 40. He was a professor in Visegrad. And Drago Gavrilovic, age 40, worked at the hydroelectric plant. Three, Boban Tomic. Four, Dragan Tomic were making lists of the members of the ethnic Muslim community to be executed and detained." Did you say these names? And Risto Perisic was included.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: No, no, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Did you mention Tomic, either Dragan and Boban?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: I mentioned Dragan Tomic and that brother of his, Risto, Esad Gadzo, but it was the SDS, not the Muslims. They weren't with the Muslims. They were the SDS.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And could we please go to page 6 of the English translation. And, Your Honour, we are still in private session. I don't believe we need to be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Open session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And page 4 of the B/C/S statement is the coordinating page according to the reference.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: There's a sentence stating: "I do not remember the names of the remaining three persons who were killed," and this is in reference to ten people killed June 10th, 1992, at the Varda factory. And according to the proofing note, you state that you do not understand the question because you do know who was killed, and namely the persons that were killed was your husband, Ahmet and Mr. Kasapovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And Mr. Karaman; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. That's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: So regardless, in 1993, the interviewer failed to note that you knew those people at Varda; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: I knew those people, the ones you've just enumerated, Kasapovic, Ramovic, and my husband.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But, ma'am, in your proofing note or any statements after, there's no clarification or mention that you in fact witnessed the abduction and/or death of these ten people. Can you explain that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: How do you mean abducted? They were forced to leave the sawmill and then were killed. They were forced. They weren't abducted. That's what I'm saying. I don't know how else to say it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: What I'm saying, ma'am, is there's just simply no mention in the 1993 statement that you were a direct eyewitness to these men being forced --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: I always made that same statement. The statement is always the same, and it has to be the same, and it cannot be any other way. I said what I saw. I couldn't have seen anything else. And if you were -- had you been where I was, you would have seen the same thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But, ma'am, the question I asked is: Can you explain why the 1993 statement of you does not mention that you witnessed the ten people at Varda being killed personally?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: I have absolutely no idea why it's not there. It should be. I always gave the same statement. I'll never forget that statement, because I am afraid to the present day. I'm always afraid when I have to make that statement and say those things, and I'll always have that image in my mind, imprinted in my mind and before my eyes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Could the court assistant please go to page 4 in B/C/S -- excuse me, page 5 in B/C/S and page 8 in English, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And according to this, ma'am, that you corrected the spelling of the name from Behra to Behija Zukic, number 1, in terms of -- in reference to: "I am also familiar with the fact that more citizens of Muslim nationality were killed in June 1992. Their names are as follows: Number 1, Behra Zukic, aged around 38, killed in her house in Dusce settlement."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And you corrected the spelling; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: I don't know how I corrected that. You have to explain that me. You have to show it to me so that I know what I corrected.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I apologise, ma'am, for -- you corrected how her name was said; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: Oh, I see. That you mean. Some called her Behija. Others called her Behka, but I think her real name is Behija, and people would use the term of endearment, Behka.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And my next question is, ma'am, if you were given an opportunity to clarify in 2008 and also gave statements in -- in -- excuse me, in your proofing statement September 21st, 2008, why didn't you clarify that there was no mention of you witnessing the -- first the seizure of Ms. Zukic's car right in front of you as you stated earlier on direct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: Who says it's always the same statement? I always said the same thing. I can't change a statement when that's what I know. I can't say that Milan went to kill someone else and then to lie and say something that I didn't see. I'll never do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Ma'am, can you explain why the 1993 statement doesn't include the information that you saw Behija Zukic's car taken from her?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: How do I know that? How can I explain that? I always made the same statement, always the same statement. Because I was there on the spot, so I can't say anything other than what I saw.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And the only other corrections that you gave, though, with regard to the 1993 statement were corrections on the killing of Mr. Musevic, Dervis Musevic and Rusta Musevic, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: That's correct, but that was afterwards, after the people who were taken. This was later, perhaps three days later. After everything that happened and then still later.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And according to your clarification or your proofing note, the only other correction you had related to page 6 B/C/S, page 10 English, was from the list of girls taken away, the witness was only familiar with the two girls Repuhsevici [sic].

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: Repuha, her daughter-in-law and daughter. We were in Muja Zulcic's house. We all collected there together. We thought that we would be safer if there were more of us together, but it was worse, and we were at Muja Zulcic's, Mustafa's. And then they came from Repusovic and he was expelled and they came from Musa Zulcic, and that evening when he arrived, his daughter was taken away and his daughter-in-law. They were taken to Vilina Vlas, and I was in the house that very night. So I'm an eyewitness to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And so, ma'am, you had no other clarifications in your September 21st proofing note than the ones we've talked about here today; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: I don't know what you mean. What I just said is the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, at this point I would tender the 14 December 1993 statement, 1D10-2087 for the English version and 1D10-2099 for the B/C/S version into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It is admitted as Exhibit number 1D66 under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And we -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Okay, ma'am. Now the next thing I'd like to refer to and I'd like to pull up 1D10-2106 and 1D10-2111 referencing the January 14th, 1994 statement. Now, do you recall giving a statement about a month later?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: How do you mean? What year? You mean this month?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: No, January 1994, ma'am. We just talked about December 1993, and I'm asking you about January 1994. Just about a month later.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: I can't remember. I can't remember January or the date or anything. All I remember is the experience, what I lived through, where I was, and I remember that very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, at this point in time you now state that you witnessed the killing of ten Visegrad residents employed at the Varda at around 12.00 noon; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: I always remember that. I'll never forget that and it's difficult for me to remember it now, too. I have sleepless nights thinking about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, in your 1994 statement you only made two clarifications. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: I don't know what statement that was. Explain it to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, accord -- let me just -- let me just read from you, and we can go to -- I guess it would be page 2 in the B/C/S, page 2 in the English. Now, according to this statement, the Passat arrived, and Milan Lukic went into the sawmill, entered it and came out with ten employees all together. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: What mill? What mill did you say?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: The sawmill, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: Yes, the sawmill. That's right. He entered the sawmill, and he came with the people. He forced them to the gate just like sheep. Ibrisim Memisevic took off his shirt there at the gate, and they took out his documents, keys -- they took out keys, cigarettes, the keys to the cupboards where they kept their uniforms and they threw it all on to that shirt. Then he made them go down towards the Drina just like sheep. He herded them like sheep in front of him. And Osmanagic Hamed, put his arm around his -- threw his arm around his shoulder, threw him down to the Drina and then he spaced them out and started killing them one by one. And when he killed them all, he went back and shot a burst of gun-fire at them.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, at them, who's "them," ma'am?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: Those people there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Who did he -- who did he shoot at? It says: "He went back and shot a burst of gun-fire at them." Who do you mean?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: Well, my neighbours from the sawmill, the ones he took away. The ones that I just told you of, that I enumerated.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, ma'am, according to the proofing note, you made a clarification that Milan Lukic took all of the prisoners to the Drina at the same time not in two different groups as it indicates in the statement, page 2 in B/C/S, page 2 in English. Is that -- so you clarified that; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: I always said that he took them down to the river all together, and this group of three people had been taken away by him beforehand, before. Then he came back to fetch the other people and forced them to go down to the river.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: If we could just redact her husband's name if we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, redact that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And so, ma'am, why I'm confused is, is because today on direct examination you indicated that it was actually seven people at noon and the three unnamed was, in fact, your husband and the two other gentlemen. But according to the 1994 statement, it appears that a total of 13 people were removed from the Varda that morning.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: I'll count the people and the names and you write them down. You make a note of them. Can we do it that way? I'll name the names and you make a note of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, ma'am, I'm just going from the statement that states: "I stated earlier that I could only remember seven of the people who were led out and killed. Their names are as follows: Ibrisim Memisevic" --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: Not Ibrahim but Ibrisim.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes, ma'am. Who else? Why don't you name them for me?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: There you go, one by one. Ramiz Karaman, Podzic Mujo, Ahmet Kasapovic, taken at half past 10.00 from the Varda sawmill, taken back into town. They came back. I didn't check my watch. And I always said that. I didn't check my watch. Was it half past 11.00? Was it noon? The Passat came back the same place as before, parked the same place as before, Milan Lukic got out, went over to the management building. They were probably having breakfast there. He picked up all the people, drove them as far as the gate, from the gate onto the Drina riverbank and killed them right there. I gave a statement about that too. I stand by that statement. This is something that I saw with my very own eyes, and nobody can tell me otherwise.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But, ma'am, according to the 1998 -- excuse me, 1994 statement, it appears that in the group at noon there were ten people, three unnamed, seven you could name. Do you understand why I'm confused?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: I understand what you're saying. You might find it confusing that I didn't mention those three names; right? Is that what you find confusing? That's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: No, I find confusing that it appears that there's three extra people that were brought out of the Varda factory, simply three that can't be named.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: I can't say. Those three men down there, perhaps someone wrote down. It's the three that I said including my husband and those other two.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, just a technical note. Our LiveNote stopped working. We're using the public screen at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I'll ask the court deputy to have the technical people look into that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And, ma'am, according to the proofing note of September 21st, 2008, the only other clarification you had for the 1994 statement was that Milan Lukic allegedly put his hand -- excuse me, Milan Lukic put his arm around Hamed, not Musan; is that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: I think it was Hamed Osmanagic that he put his hand around as they were headed down towards the Drina, and the others were walking in front of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time I would tender the January 14th, 1994, statement, 1D10-2106, into evidence with the B/C/S statement 1D10-2111.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, and you have about four minutes, Mr. Alarid.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the statement is admitted as Exhibit number 1D67, under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Just a moment, Your Honour. Just a moment, Judge.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Can you describe how Milan Lukic looked when he was at the Varda factory?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: I can. Camouflage uniform. That's what he was wearing. Thin. He wasn't fat, he was thin.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: How old did you believe him to be?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: Over 40, but I don't know exactly. It's difficult for me to get dates right or someone's age. I just don't know. Over 40. I'm sure he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, ma'am, if he was eight or ten years old when you were still a girl, right about the time you got married, he would have to be 40, wouldn't he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: I said that, too, but I wasn't sure about the age when I said it either.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, the only way you could have seen him on the bus would have been had this been before you moved to Visegrad; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: That's right. I was a young girl. Milan was just a small boy. He was school age. He went to school, and that's how I got to know him. He was watching the cattle because that's what children out in the country did. He can tell you himself if that's true or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You must bring the cross-examination to an end now.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I was, Your Honour, and the only thing I'd want to do other than that is admit the witness statement of 17 October 1998 to the ICTY, which is uploaded as 1D10-2115 and 1D10-2120.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, we admit those.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit number 1D68, under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And I would also admit the statement of 14 April 2008 as 1D10-2131, and B/C/S version is 1D10-2138, also to the ICTY.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: No further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It is admitted as Exhibit number 1D69, under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, madam.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Let me introduce myself my name is Djuro Cepic. I defend Mr. Sredoje Lukic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: Pleased to meet you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you to please listen carefully to my --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: Well, if you ask me clear questions and I can focus, I'll make sure to provide good answers for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Can we please now go back to the situation when the Uzice Corps entered Visegrad. At the time you were not in town yourself. You only arrived later with your husband and two sons; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: What do you mean the Uzice Corps entering Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Well, you said that today, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: Yes. I went to Rogatica and then I was back, but before that I was in Visegrad. I spent more time in Visegrad than I was away for.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I want to know about the situation when you went back to Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Just clarify everything you've got, and I'll explain how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Is it true that there were considerable numbers of Muslims who were hiding in the woods, many of them in their basements and other places, too, in order to keep safe; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: No, no, no. That wasn't true. People went to work. They never hid anywhere. There was nothing like that, nothing of the kind you suggest in your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Upon your return to Visegrad, did you go back to your family home in Dusce?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: Yes. I went back from Rogatica six days later.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Isn't it true that at the time there was a curfew that had been imposed; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: Yes, that's true. There was a curfew. We couldn't leave or go anywhere. People were standing guard. There were several points at which they were standing guard. On the way back from Rogatica, they harassed us, Where are you off to, where are you going, give us your weapons. All sorts of mistreatments. Let me not even begin to tell you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And it was because of such mistreatment that you never left Dusce. You stayed at home with your family and your husband would go to work to the Varda factory?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: Yes, he would always go to work because Behija had received every guarantee that he would be safe. Stanko Pecikoza, in front of me, told him that he would be safe. He guaranteed that.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: But it was difficult to move about beyond that because there were barricades, check-points. It was impossible because one wanted to avoid humiliation, didn't one?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: There was always humiliation. There was always mistreatment. If you put all of my experience together, you could get a very good novel out of it, I expect.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: That much is clear. Thank you very much. That situation continued until the time you left Visegrad; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: Yes. It was always like that. Mistreatment down to the last day when I left Visegrad on a convoy. I went as far as Bikavac. I spent three days in the woods. I didn't even dare go home. Milan Lukic was out to get me. My mother-in-law told me. She's dead. She died. When I left that group, I went down to the gate to ask Stanko Pecikoza, (redacted)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. May I continue?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: Sredoje was my friend too. We were on visiting terms, but my son's friend. They worked together. He was like he was my own son. Whenever I gave my son a drink, I'd give Sredoje one. Whenever I gave my son something to eat, and -- and then he would joke many times. He'd say, You Muslims should be killed like flies, and we would just laugh, you know, but it was jestful. He was saying this as a joke, you know. He said, You Muslims, you should be done away with. But eventually he ended up doing what he'd been promising all these years.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: He and your son were great friends, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: Yes. They were great friends because my son was a good person. He was not a wicked person. He loved Sredoje as though Sredoje were his own brother. Why didn't Sredoje do anything for his father, to make sure Milan didn't kill him, if they were friends? That's what I'm asking you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: All right. We're getting to that, but he was good friends with your husband too?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: He was friends with all of us. We were on visiting terms. We would go visit them at their home and that sort of thing. And why did he do that? I'm asking you that. Why he do that?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You would help each other out, building your homes, that sort of thing, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: What do you mean?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: Yes. My husband was quite good at this and he was a very good man. He was famous for that, and we were a famous family for being as good we were. I think the only thing that really mattered was my husband was a Muslim. And then sometimes when Bajram came, he would fast. I think that's what everybody was bothered by, but that was the only thing they could have possibly minded because they never even harmed a fly, not my children, not my husband, not no one.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you very much. Can you just keep your answers short.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: Yes. Whatever I know, I'll tell you. I'll tell you the truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: You were furious about Sredoje because he wasn't there to help your husband and your son later on when they needed help?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: Furious, why? Can you explain that?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: You were furious, you were mad with Sredoje because he wasn't there to help your son Fikret when Fikret come to grief?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: He wouldn't have helped him out. He would have killed him like he killed his father, right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... are we in private or?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open and I'm making two more redactions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You just mentioned the son's name.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Mm-hmm. Oh, I kindly ask redaction of the names, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, we'll have those redacted.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam, you remember the statement that you gave, the first statement you made to the OTP, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: You read it for me so I make sure what it was that I said. And I'm going to tell you one thing: It's true. I never said anything but the truth, the very truth. That's all I ever said.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Exhibit number 1D68, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam, as we're waiting for the exhibit to come up, you will agree with this: When Sredoje came to visit you, there was always a friendly atmosphere always, full of friendship between your son and Sredoje Lukic, wouldn't you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: Yes. The atmosphere was like that. But what did Sredoje do, I'm asking you? He did what he did. That's what he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: We'll be coming to that later on. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Maybe it could be easy if I gave ERN number 2D02-0221, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam, I will read a portion of this to you and then you can comment.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: Sure. Whatever I know. You just need to make it neat for me so I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I would just like to ask you to focus on my questions and answer them. Can we please have page 3 in the B/C/S. [Previous translation continues] ... [In English] ... in B/C/S. Third paragraph in English, fourth paragraph in B/C/S. [Interpretation] You say that driver was sitting in the car. It was a dark red Passat, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: Which driver?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: And you said: "I assume that the driver was his brother."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: Sredoje Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Because they were always together?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: Yes. They were always together.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Therefore you will agree with me that you did not see that. It was merely an assumption on your part, as you state?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: I didn't look him in the eye. I didn't dare to look because as soon as you had a look at them, they would shoot straight away.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Transcript, transcript.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Transcript, transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: So for fear of not being yet another victim, you didn't even look that way, did you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: No, not at the car, not at the Fico. I saw Milan walk up to the car, Dzemo Zukic leave the car, and Behka, Behija Zukic, and then we all walked on together towards Varda.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: But out of fear, you didn't see the driver in the Fico, in the other red car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: Yes. He was sitting in the Fico, in the Fiat car.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Madam, but there's none of that in your statement. How come all the changes today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: I always said the same thing. I don't know why it's not in the statement. What I say, I maintain. That's how I was brought up.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you about the Varda factory, and in front of the Varda, the first day of the Bajram holiday?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: On the eve of Bajram.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Yes, on the eve of Bajram. You didn't see who was in the vehicle, and you clearly said that in your statement. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: I didn't personally see. Two men, Sredoje Lukic and Milan Lukic were driving the Passat from Dzemo Zukic and nobody else ever drove that car.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But you personally didn't see them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: I did. Personally from my terrace I saw it.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: We'll come to that, but thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Could we have --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Were you watching from the terrace or from the veranda?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: From the terrace. I indicated with an arrow where I was. I had several terraces, not just one. Sredoje Lukic knows very well how many terraces I had.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Could we have 1D69, or if it's easier to find in e-court system 2D02-0256, the witness statement from 14th of April, 2008.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam, do you remember that you talked to the representatives of the OTP in April?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: I don't know who I talked to. I talked to lots of people because I talk to everybody. I don't know what the date was. I don't remember any of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... [overlapping speakers]... please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll read it out, the last sentence in paragraph 9 of your statement. You're describing everything that happened and then you say: "Milan Lukic entered the car. The driver was there too, but I did not see who that was. They drove by my house on their way towards town." Has that refreshed your memory, madam?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: Well, what did you say? When they got to the gate to take the people away? Is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I'll read the whole paragraph if you find it easier.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: Well, of course it's easier. Now I'm telling you what I'm telling you and that's how it was. That's how I must say it. So there's no need looking at me. It was like it was just as I'm sitting here now.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Madam, just short answers, please. You say: "I saw Milan Lukic enter the gate and saw Rasim Karaman exit the administration building."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: Ramiz Karaman is his name.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: And you can see the administration building from your terrace. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: You can see everything, absolutely everything.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And then you go on to say that Milan Lukic told Ahmed and Ramiz to wait by the car, and then you state that Milan Lukic got into the car and that a driver was there, but you didn't see who it was. Now let's focus on the administrative building as you see it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: Yes, let's focus on that, and I'll tell you how it was, and you listen to me carefully because it's the way I say it. You weren't there. I was there and I know exactly how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: May I ask you something, madam?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: Yes. You can ask me and you can ask me to repeat what I said and I'll repeat exactly how it was. You want me to say it one more time to make it even clearer?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Madam, please, I'm here to ask the questions.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: You're asking me questions I don't understand and I keep telling you the same thing, the way it must be. Now you're putting me right, but it's not how you want to hear it, it's how I'm saying it.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have to say that we haven't got LiveNote system. Actually, my assistant haven't got that system.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: There seems to be another technical problem with the LiveNote. I'll ask the technical people to attend to that. Let us proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Could we have in e-court system P157, please. Could we have zoom out, please. Do you recall a different exhibit 1 -- P153, please. We have a better view.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam, we can see Dusce here?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: We can see your house, the big house. Now, would you point, if you can, and draw the direction of the administrative building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: Yes, I can do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Now, that small little house next to the building, is that what you mean?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: No. This is the office building.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: And what -- where's the administrative building where the other people are?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: Over here.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: How far is it from here?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: Well, not far. The gutter is over here and that's where the people were taken. Now, let me show you where he took my husband.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Listen to my question carefully.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: I am not literate. I'm telling you what I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: You mentioned the administration building on the Varda factory.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: The Varda factory was further away. I just mentioned these offices here from where my husband was taken, but the furniture factory was down, further down where Milan took the Passat from Dzemo Zukic and then you have the sawmill. That's further off.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Could we have an exhibit number for this photo, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Do you want to have that admitted?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. We admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit number 2D21, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Could we have -- zoom in on this photo, and the house, if possible, as big as possible. Your Honour, if I may know what time will be break, just to consider my questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Five minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam, now we can see your house better. Can we zoom in a bit more?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: Thank you. I can see it very well too.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: If it's possible on the right side. Just a little bit more, one centimetre or two. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now we can see your house there. Could you tell me -- I can see two terraces. Am I right that you have an upper and a lower terrace?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: Yes, you are right.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Were they red painted metal railings to the terraces?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, red painted metal.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: And what about the door, the door going out into the terrace, was it a wooden door?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Were they wooden doors?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: What about the upper storey where that window is just under the roof? Were they wooden boards or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: No, they weren't wooden boards.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you make a circle around the upper terrace to your house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: You mean this one up here?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Yes. Is that where you were and observed things?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: Yes, and that's where I lived.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you put a B next to the balcony, just beside it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: I can't write anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: All right. An X then, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: That's fine.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: I don't know if I managed to mark that properly.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: So that's the upper terrace where you were standing and watching everything?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: Yes, when my husband was taken and all the rest of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It's admitted as 2D22, under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: May I ask Madam Usher to distribute this. Could we have one for witness, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Perhaps we could just go into closed session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] While we're waiting for this to come up, madam, let me ask you this: Are you not a member of the association known as Women Victims Of The War led by Bakira Hasecic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: No, that's not true. I'm not a member of any association. All I want to know in this world is my household and my children. I am a homemaker.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Witness, on cross-examination you were asked some questions about statements that you gave in Visoko. Can you describe for the Court the conditions under which those statements were given?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: I gave some statements. Some people came over, several different groups, to see how we lived as refugees and for us to tell them more about how exactly this happened, who was killed, who lost whom. So we gave statements about all of these. And it wasn't just me. There were thousands and thousands of souls from Foca, from Visegrad, from all over, Visoko, Munstra [phoen]. Thousands and thousands of souls. We were packed like sardines in a tin can. We had nowhere to even lie down. We would lie down on the floor. My kidneys were ruined, and I had no idea at the time what had become of any of my nearest and dearest. Just to remember that day, we had to leave on convoys and how we were mistreated in all sorts of ways.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: If I could just direct you more specifically to the occasions upon which you gave these statements. Do you remember how many people were present as witnesses when you were giving these statements?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: Believe it or not, there would have to be 20, 30 people even in those halls, what have you, rooms. Those were classrooms in a school, and then depends on how many people happened to sit in on an interview, and then everybody had something to say. They gave us paper to write things down with a pen. That's how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Your Honour, could we move into open session if we're currently in private session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Open session, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: You said that there were many people --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Witness, you said that there were many people present in these interviews. Was information taken down from all of these many witnesses?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: Believe me, I don't know. I was hardly in touch with anyone. I had my grandchildren. I socialised with them. I spent my time with them, not anyone else. I'm sure there are more people who should make statements. I'm sure there are people who refused to make statements because they're afraid. I'm not afraid. I stop at nothing. I am here to tell the truth because that is my only motive. My only ambition, to tell the truth. And I'd never talk about stuff that I didn't see. There were other people who were killed in Musici and other villages, but I wasn't there, was I? So I'm not going to be telling you about that. I'm going to be telling you about my village.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Could the court officer bring up Exhibit 1D66, the B/C/S version on the left side of e-court and Exhibit 1D69 on the right side of e-court. Sorry, the English version of 1D69, and zoom in on the signatures at the bottom of each page.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Witness, can you see the two statements on the screen in front of you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: Yes. I don't know what it says though. I see, but I can't read it because I didn't go to school. I see that I signed this.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: And which of those two statements did you sign?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: This one.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Would that be the statement on the right or the left?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: Yes, yes, on the right.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: And the signature on the statement on the left, is that your signature?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: No. I don't know how to do that. I can't sign a document like that. I didn't go to school. This is as much as I learned, just to mark it, as it were.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Could the court officer please bring up Exhibit 1D67 on the left side. And it looks like it's actually been brought up on the right side of e-court, which is fine, but could we zoom in on the signature at the bottom of the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Witness, looking at the signature on the bottom of the page on the right side in e-court, is that your signature?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: No. I wasn't able to sign it like that. Maybe I gave someone my ID, because we were several witnesses there when these things were signed, but I don't know. I told you there were several of us in a room each time the statements were given and when we told our story.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, you've been wearing eye-glasses in court today. Do you use those glasses to see things up close or at a distance?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: Up close, up close. When something needs doing back at home, for example, if I'm cooking lunch, then I have to put my glasses on.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: What was the condition of your eyesight in 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-042
utterances.text: Great, couldn't be better. I was exceptionally healthy. Sredoje Lukic can tell you what I looked like at the time. I never thought that anything like this would strike me.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: I think Mr. Cepic may have something to say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, with your leave I think last two or three questions are not raised from the cross-examination. This is something different.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Your Honour, cross-examination focused on the ability of the witness to accurately observe events at a distance, so I think that it does in fact arise out of cross.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I agree, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Could we move into private session for a few questions?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Alarid.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Simply in a response to the designation, I believe that it's proper for viva voce; namely, not just the points Mr. Groome brought up but also we were disclosed as part of the batch that on the 26th of October, 2008, there is an additional witness statement which is -- involves clarifications of the 2000 statement that go into quite a bit of detail and quite a bit of changes, in fact. And considering the fact that you need to lay a foundation that earlier statements would be the same as if written today, simply that clearly they weren't as of October 26th as several -- these clarifications were made to her statement and she signed this statement as well, but I think all -- all in all, it goes to show that the earlier statements needed clarification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: What is the time estimate for this witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honour, if we were permitted to call her 92 ter it would be approximately 30 minutes. If we were required to call her viva voce, I believe it would probably be about two hours. And just to respond to what Mr. Alarid said, I was going to make a submission on this. The witness had several clarifications to her one ICTY statement. We endeavoured, in order to save time in court, to prepare that as an addendum statement with clarifications. I'd be perfectly happy to lead those additional clarifications viva voce as part of a 92 ter process, or to submit that one page addendum statement which contains the minor clarifications. So the intention was to seek to admit her ICTY statement pursuant to Rule 92 ter and then to seek to admit the few clarifications that she made to that statement in order to facilitate things and make the process as efficient as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And that would be half an hour?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes. If the statement were accepted as such, yes, Your Honour, that would be approximately half an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And you will have an opportunity to cross-examine, of course, under 92 ter, both counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We will hear the evidence under 92 ter. Let the witness make the declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You may sit. And you may begin, Ms. Marcus.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Could I request that the pseudonym sheet be shown to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Madam Witness, can you hear me clearly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: You've been granted protective measures of a pseudonym and your face -- and your face is being distorted for the purposes of these proceedings. Can you confirm that your name and date of birth appear on the paper in front of you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Could you kindly sign that paper.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: I'd like to request that the court officer to show that to the Defence and to the Chamber, and then I'd like to tender that into evidence under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will become Exhibit number P158, under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: I'd also like to request the court officer to please provide the witness with a reference sheet.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Madam Witness, the paper in front of you will contain the names of other persons who have also been granted protective measures by this Tribunal. Therefore, I request that if you were to name them in your testimony that you kindly use their pseudonym that you see on the page in front of you rather than their names. Do you understand?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: VG-064, can you tell us where you were born?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064
utterances.text: I was born in Dobrun, Visegrad municipality.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness kindly be asked to speak up, please, and approach the microphones. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Madam Witness, you've been requested to -- if you could, to move forward slightly so the microphones can pick up what you're saying.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064
utterances.text: Yes. Can you hear me now?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Are you married?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Do you have any children?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064
utterances.text: I do, two.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: What is your profession?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064
utterances.text: I'm a saleswoman, salesperson.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Do you recall giving a statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: To the -- do you recall giving a statement to the Tribunal on Sunday, the 26th of October, 2008? That would be yesterday.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Was that -- I see my colleague on his feet?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I apologise but we haven't got -- received any statement. We just received the proofing note.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: And that was yesterday. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honour, the draft was sent yesterday at the end of the proofing session, immediately after receiving the information. And in the e-mail that the proofing note was attached to, we informed Defence counsel that we would be formalising it into an addendum statement, again in an effort to expedite the process of making the minor clarifications and saving the time for the substantive matters. So this morning the statement was finalised and signed, translated into B/C/S and sent to the Defence this morning. May I continue, Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. I'm really cogitating on this recurring problem. So they have -- the statement was in fact sent to them.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. This is a proofing note but because -- it's basically a proofing note -- but in order to save -- I see we're using court time now discussing it, so I'll be happy to lead these corrections live, but they're corrections like instead of the word "to" it should be "toward." And in order to just expedite the process and save the precious 30 minutes for the substance, we just prepared it in the form of a signed statement which we'll seek to admit with the statement. That's all. It's just clarification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Very well, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: So, Madam Witness, did you give a statement to the Tribunal yesterday, the 26th of October, 2008?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Was the statement read back to you in the Bosnian language?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Did you sign that statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: If I were to ask you the same questions now which you were asked in providing that statement, would your answers be the same?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would like to tender the statement of the 26th of October, 2008, into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Alarid.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: -- something that would have come in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Madam Witness, did you give a statement to investigators of the ICTY on the 14th of May and 13th of June of the year 2000?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Did you have an opportunity to review that statement in the Bosnian language before coming to court today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Could I request the court officer to please call up 65 ter number 124. And that would be e-court page 5. I'm sorry, let's begin -- let's begin on the front cover. I'm sorry. Just the front page.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: VG-064, do you see the page on the screen in front of you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Do you see your date of birth there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Is that your correct date of birth?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064
utterances.text: No. It says the 12th of October, and I was born on the 17th of October.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we go now to page 4 in the English. To the bottom paragraph on that page. Madam Witness, do you see the paragraph that begins with the words: "The last time I went there was on the 25th of June 1992"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064
utterances.text: What did you say? I didn't understand you because the screen was moving.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Do you see a paragraph at the bottom of that page which begins with the words: "The last time I went there was on 25th of June 1992"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Can you read the line right after that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064
utterances.text: Yes. "On that day, I was supposed to leave Visegrad on a convoy to the small town of Visoko." It should say to Kladanj and Olovo, not Visoko.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we now please turn to page 7 of the English statement. The first paragraph. I'm just waiting for the corresponding Bosnian version. Madam Witness, in the top paragraph you say the words: "At that time, Fikreta was two months pregnant."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064
utterances.text: No, she was four months pregnant.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we turn to page 8, please, in the English. Down to paragraph five. Madam Witness, there's a line on this page which says: "Then Milan Lukic entered the house where we were detained and took out --" I'd like to go into private session. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Private session, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your statements have been entered into evidence, and thus, I will not be going through the entirety of your experiences during this court hearing. However, I will ask you a few questions on a few matters which you raise in your statement. Excuse me one moment. In the spring of 1992 when the war began, where did you reside?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064
utterances.text: I lived in the village of Musici, Visegrad municipality.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Where is Musici in relation to the town of Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064
utterances.text: It's five kilometres away from Visegrad towards Visegradska Banja or spa. And you turn left there -- well, anyways, it's five kilometres away from Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Did you live with anyone?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064
utterances.text: I lived with my husband and two children.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Now, I don't know if the statement is still up, but I would like to return to this statement. It's P159. Could I request e-court page 5 in the English and page 4 in the Bosnian, B/C/S. In the middle of the page, please. Madam Witness, I'd like to ask you to read for us two paragraphs from your statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: And for this I'm afraid, Your Honours, we'll need to go into private session again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in private session.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Please begin with the paragraph starting: "In the late afternoon on the same day, another group ..." Do you see where I'm referring to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Please read -- please kindly read that paragraph and the following one.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064
utterances.text: "In the late afternoon on the same day, another group of 15 armed men and one woman arrived in the village of Musici. The group was driving a BMW, a VW, our own car, 128, and a Yugo. The men had black painted faces and some were wearing a fur hat with a cockade on, the so-called Subara. They also brought with them a black flag with a skull and bones. "The members of the group ordered all inhabitants of the village to gather in the house of my father-in-law (redacted). The leader of the group gave a speech there. First he introduced himself as Milan Lukic and then he introduced his group and said, This is my police. Then he asked about the shooting from the village of Musici on police patrols passing by the village. There were some verbal threats too. Then he counted us. I don't remember how many we were. And finally he promised to protect us. He had blue jeans on and a black shirt. He also had a cap with a skull and -- on his head. Well, it wasn't a cap, it was a hat, and he had black stripes on his face."

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: In the section you just read, you mentioned that the group came in a BMW, a Volkswagen, your own car, and a Yugo. Are those all the cars that you recall seeing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064
utterances.text: I saw -- well, there was Behija Zukic's Passat in a burgundy colour, but it's not mentioned there. And that car was driven by Milan Lukic personally.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: How do you know --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Ms. Marcus, I'm sorry to stop you but it's after the time for us to break. So we're going to adjourn now and we'll resume tomorrow at 2.15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 28th day of October, 2008, at 2.15 p.m.
